source.title: BEAN: Interpretable Representation Learning with Biologically-Enhanced Artificial Neuronal Assembly Regularization
source.authors: Yuyang Gao; Giorgio A. Ascoli; Liang Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The study measures interpretability-related outcomes using neuron clustering and group ablation, but these are population-level measures and do not test whether individual neuron poles have one main job or the share of poles that are understood.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own interpretability-related outcomes, but they concern learned neuron assemblies and class-selective groups rather than the individual-neuron claims in V1–V7. These findings are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study proposes BEAN, a regularizer that deliberately induces neuronal assemblies in the dense layers of small image classifiers (MLP, LeNet-5, ResNet18 on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10). It measures population-level clustering (Silhouette index) and group-ablation selectivity. It does not audit how many individual neurons have one main job or how many are understood. It studies no language models, no InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons, no attribution graphs, and does not score explanations against held-out activations. Because the structure is induced on purpose by a purpose-built loss, it does not test V4's claim that the share of interpretable neurons rises with modern architectures and tools. It neither tests nor relies on the claim, so the reader's 'tests/T2' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that BEAN yields interpretable, class-aligned neuronal assemblies and sparse, efficient dense layers without accuracy loss, and that it improves few-shot learning from scratch. The group-ablation selectivity–importance link is clearest for BEAN-2. They make no claim about the share of individual neurons with one main job.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image-classification networks with BEAN regularization and evaluates clustering and group ablation; it does not use the neuron-pole auditing or explanation-testing procedures described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that BEAN-2 produces a clearer selectivity–importance association than BEAN-1 in group ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: BEAN-1/BEAN-2 raise Silhouette indices of dense-layer neuron clustering from about 0.55–0.59 (vanilla) to about 0.84–0.94.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Assembly-promoting regularization makes the last dense layer's neurons form class-aligned clusters in small image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: In vanilla LeNet-5 on MNIST, class-selective neuron groups show no clear selectivity–importance link under group ablation; with BEAN-2 the link clearly emerges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization toward neuronal assemblies can make class-selective neuron groups causally important for their class.

record.problems: The interpretability-related evidence is based on population-level clustering and group ablation, not tested explanations of individual neurons. Silhouette results are reported approximately in prose, and the ablation interpretation is qualitative; no uncertainty is stated for these results.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B, no neuron-pole audit, no shares by number of jobs.
No language models, no dense vs MoE comparison, no scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, no pose or recursive-generalization analysis.
No share of individually interpretable neurons. No comparison of architectures or tools. A regularizer induces assemblies on purpose, which does not test the claim.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of activating-example explanations against firing predictions.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche were corrected from tests/T2 to discusses/T6. 'Discusses' is the closest available label, although the paper does not discuss this claim at all. The prose 'around 0.9' overstates some Figure 2 Silhouette values (about 0.84). Efficiency (Table 1) and few-shot (Table 2) results are irrelevant to the claim and were rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B, neuron poles, or proportions of poles by number of jobs or level of understanding.
No comparison of neuron-pole job shares across language models, model sizes, dense versus mixture-of-experts architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, shared pose features, recursive generalization, or superposition.

The study evaluates BEAN regularization's effects on neuron assemblies, but does not estimate a share of individually interpretable neurons, compare modern architectures with older ones, or test the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons explain its behavior without a trained replacement model.
No test of explanations written from activating examples against held-out activations or firing predictions.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: models evaluated (MLP, LeNet-5, ResNet18; aggregate result as described in text)
rows.operation_detail: Applied BEAN-1 regularization during training and assessed clustering of neurons in dense-layer outgoing-weight space.

conditions.value: various evaluated models on MNIST and CIFAR-10; aggregate statement

rows.baseline: Conventional DNN models with the same architectures: indices near 0.5
rows.note: The text gives approximate aggregate values for multiple models and datasets, not separate numerical results for each model.
rows.check: Subject is wrong. Figure 2 shows MLP (MNIST) and ResNet18 (CIFAR-10), not LeNet-5. The figure gives per-model values: MLP 0.5870 vs MLP+BEAN-1 0.8379; ResNet18 0.5512 vs ResNet18+BEAN-1 0.8717 (pairing of panel values is approximate from the extracted text). These are closer to 0.84–0.87 than to the prose's 'around 0.9'. The row measures induced clustering, not any claim version.

rows.operation_detail: Applied BEAN-2 regularization during training and assessed clustering of neurons in dense-layer outgoing-weight space.

conditions.value: various evaluated models on MNIST and CIFAR-10; aggregate statement

rows.baseline: Conventional DNN models with the same architectures: indices near 0.5
rows.note: The text gives approximate aggregate values for multiple models and datasets, not separate numerical results for each model.
rows.check: Same subject issue as R1. Figure 2 values for BEAN-2 are about 0.84–0.94 (MLP+BEAN-2 about 0.8418; ResNet18+BEAN-2 about 0.9442, per panel order). This is a population-level clustering measure; it bears on no version.

rows.subject: Vanilla LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Ablated one neuron group at a time, with groups identified by most selective class, and recorded class-specific performance changes.
rows.measure: Association between neuron class selectivity and importance to overall model performance under group ablation
rows.value: The authors report no clear association between neuron selectivity and importance to overall model performance.
rows.note: The reported result is qualitative; the figure shows class-specific performance changes but the text does not give numeric values.
rows.check: Qualitative only, and it echoes Morcos et al. Group-level ablation is not an individual-neuron explanation test.

rows.subject: LeNet-5+BEAN-1
rows.operation_detail: Ablated one neuron group at a time, with groups identified by most selective class, and recorded class-specific performance changes.
rows.measure: Association between neuron class selectivity and importance to overall model performance under group ablation
rows.baseline: Vanilla LeNet-5: no clear association reported
rows.value: The text reports that an association emerged when BEAN regularization was used; it does not separately characterize BEAN-1's result.
rows.note: The authors say the association was especially clear for BEAN-2, so the text gives limited variant-specific detail for BEAN-1.
rows.check: The text does not characterize BEAN-1 separately; it says only 'especially for BEAN-2'. 'Partial' is not supported by any stated value.

rows.subject: LeNet-5+BEAN-2
rows.operation_detail: Ablated one neuron group at a time, with groups identified by most selective class, and recorded class-specific performance changes.
rows.measure: Association between neuron class selectivity and importance to overall model performance under group ablation
rows.baseline: Vanilla LeNet-5: no clear association reported
rows.value: The authors report that the association between class selectivity and importance clearly emerged, especially for BEAN-2.
rows.note: This is a qualitative finding about groups of neurons, not a test of individual neuron-pole explanations.
rows.check: Qualitative group-level finding; it bears on no version.
